reviews.review_title: THE VR ROAD TRIP I’VE ALWAYS WANTED!
reviews.review_description: I absolutely love Lane Rider! Instead of forcing you from one race to another, it lets you simply get in a car, follow the GPS or completely ignore it, explore busy highways and discover where the road takes you. Racing, mapping new roads, taxi, ambulance and transport jobs give the game plenty of variety. The visuals are beautiful, performance is extremely smooth, the menus are excellent and there are several control and camera options to suit different players. Add a huge selection of cars and tons of customization and this is almost exactly the kind of VR driving game I’ve always wanted. More maps, environments, weather and day/night cycles would make it even better. A fantastic surprise and an absolute VR gem!

First off I overall recommend this game. It has good replayability and a huge selection of cars to buy with in game currency that is fairly easy to earn. Graphics are solid and there is plenty of variety with the environments.

The negative, you dont have full control of the cars. It kinda locks onto the road and you can change lanes. There are literally no left turns, gps says straight or right. So it at first feels like an open world but you quickly realize you cant make a u- turn.

Id give it 5 stars if it was 10-$15. But for $20 I expect more than a phone game port. 

If you see it on sale its definitely worth picking up. Buy at your own risk for $20.

This isn’t just another arcade racer—it’s a full-bodied driving experience where every lane change, emergency brake, and high-speed drift feels weighty and intentional. The three core modes—taxi runs, ambulance rescues, and truck deliveries—each demand different skills, while the city mapping challenges add a layer of exploration. With 20 cars to unlock and customize (paint jobs, wheels, and performance tweaks), progression feels meaningful and rewarding.
The physics engine is stunningly accurate, blending Mario Kart-style / OutRun fun with simulator-grade precision. You’ll weave through gridlocked traffic, dodge cars cutting you off at the last second, and thread exits between lumbering trucks—all while deciding whether to floor it or slam the brakes. The ability to drive the wrong way on the highway (because why not?) adds a rebellious edge to the gameplay.
With inside/outside camera options and a global leaderboard to compete against others, it’s as much about mastery as it is about style. The no-nonsense progression system ensures you’re always chasing the next unlock, while the solid execution keeps every session fresh.
If you love driving games that respect your skill but still let you go wild, this is a must-play. Hours of replayability await—just don’t get too attached to your paint job when you inevitably scrape it against a guardrail. 🏁

This is such a great experience on Quest hardware. The car interiors are very detailed, and the way the sunlight casts shadows around as you drive is very impressive.
But the most jaw-dropping thing is just how far you can see in all directions when you look out the windows! The draw-distance is really good, and you really feel like you're in the midst of a bustling, living world. 
The island you drive around has so much variety, with massive suspension bridges to cross, rural areas and towns, and there's so much traffic to negotiate. It's actually amazing how much the developers have managed to cram in. 
A very enjoyable game with loads to do and different classes of cars to try out. 
I hope that maybe a night mode could be added sometime in the future, and it would be nice if the resolution could be squeezed a little higher. It runs so smoothly on Quest 3, I'm sure that would be possible. 
Very happy I found this.
Can't stop playing it!

reviews.review_title: For US motorways & lane assist lovers
reviews.review_description:
Imagine cruising down the exact same slightly curved motorway between two cities with pleasant scenery, endless identical interchanges, and heavy lane assist permanently locked on, complete with random drifting sound effects at roundabouts. That is Lane Rider: Highway Runner.

The promo promises open world freedom and intense high speed traffic weaving. In reality, the game drives for you. With auto accelerate on, you do not even steer; the road zigzags automatically, leaving you to merely twitch your position inside the lane. You can finish almost every route without touching the brakes once.

The store page hypes hundreds of kilometers of highways and multiple car classes, but most routes are just a basic four lane strip where your only job is picking right turns or straight paths. Left turns do not even exist. The vehicles feel almost identical, whether you drive a starter car or a heavy cargo truck.

Progression is a special kind of agony. You get pop up chat logs from your cousin. The text is legible, but completely un-narrated and aggressively boring to read in VR. Add a casino prize roulette, and you have peak mobile trash UI.

What passes for fun? Decent scenery, drifting audio, and cars honking when you drift into the wrong lane to give you a fake head-on scare. It is deeply relaxing if you want to zone out and stare at roadside bumpers while doing absolute zero, but as a game, it is comically hollow.

Here is a wild thought: this lifeless cruise could actually be salvageable if it embraced a roguelike structure, injecting actual stakes, random chaos, and unpredictability instead of forcing you down a mindless straight line.

If you want an arcade-ish driving game that was also ported from mobile, but built with vastly more care, thought, and actual depth, check out Mini Motor Racing X. It is much more fun, cars actually feel distinct, and the tracks offer genuine variety and driving engagement.

Otherwise, still an amazing game. Thanks again Devs, keep up the great work!

reviews.review_title: The arcade racing game I’ve been waiting
reviews.review_description:
Let's start with the gameplay and the different race types: Taxi Mode, Discovery Mode, and Time Attack. In Taxi Mode, you have to take customers from point A to point B without worrying about the clock. In Discovery Mode, you drive from one point to another, also completely stress-free without a timer. And finally, Time Attack Mode forces you to complete a race within a set time limit. Throughout the game, there is also a storyline involving your brother that features various transportation missions.
Now, to be clear: there are no races against other vehicles. It's a shame, but there is already so much to do in this game... Maybe they will add the police one day, just like in a certain Need for Speed: Hot Pursuit! The tracks are varied, and the dynamic weather changes everything, fog included. On the downside, there is no rain and no night racing. I would have absolutely loved to drive flat out down the highway in the dead of night... Maybe in a future update?
There are 24 vehicles in total, if I remember correctly. Even though it doesn't feature real, licensed brands, you can easily recognize the cars. You can customize the paint, vinyls, and even the rims. The lighting effects inside the cockpit are realistic. The other vehicles on the road are pretty well modeled, and the scenery—even if it lacks animations at times—easily immerses you in these wild highway runs.
I absolutely loved Warplanes: WW1 Fighters (a game I've been playing every single day for years!), but with this one, I think I've finally found my racing game, and I can't wait to see how it evolves. When are we getting a Bluetooth steering wheel compatible with the Meta Quest?!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
Anyway, as you can tell, I've thoroughly dissected this game and I can safely say to anyone looking for a true arcade racing experience: look no further, this is it!
Shoutout to HomeNet Games (they've made so many great games!).

reviews.review_title: Actual open world driving for quest!
reviews.review_description: Someone finally made an open world driving game for the quest, and it's actually really good! I was shocked to see the size of the map. It's actually really big for a standalone game! And the ability to clearly see landscape and buildings off into the distance is quite impressive. The developers really sell the illusion of driving through a California like map (especially with all the traffic). I'd gladly pay for more maps! My only complaint is the driving feels a bit on rails when it comes to turning and weaving through traffic. Outside of that for a standalone open world driving game, I'm very impressed!

Very nice rendered world and cars for the standalone headset. I like the campaign layout and all the things you can do. Please allow players to turn off the strong assists for steering,  drifting and breaking. At the moment you can drive around bends as fast as you want with little skill.  Manual drifting like in OutRun 2006 Coast to Coast would be much more entertaining and challenging. A score system like on Burnout games or prize money multipliers like on Test Drive Unlimited 2 when taking risks overtaking and driving on other side of the road,  Online leaders would be a good edition as well as a horn to beep and turn signals to manually apply, more cockpit interaction please. I buy all your games and know you usually release many updates so I have faith you can make this really special.

I think the cars need some tweaking though, steering feels a bit on rails and unnatural, I also think that there should be at least some major crash effects, I ran headfirst into a semi and the car just stopped with only a little noise. 

I enjoyed it overall but it doesn't feel entirely worth the price tag.

The concept is interesting, but the game itself looks very cheap and primitive. The physics are extremely basic, the car has no sense of weight and doesn’t feel real, there’s no sense of speed, and the other cars move as if they’re on rails and barely react to collisions. The world around you also feels very empty and lacking in detail. This is not something you should release for $20. In its current state, it’s worth no more than $5.
